title: push/pull
body:
you know how doors at the entry of a
building typically swing outward? like the
convention where you pull something to
enter the building and push something to
leave the building? makes sense right?
exiting should be easy 'case there's a bear
loose in the building or a fire started from a
blockhead putting a fork in the microwave.
doors should push into the most "outside" place right?
stay with me now.
the bathroom is easily the most "inside" a
room can get. it's the most private, I'd hope,
and surely not a place people want to easily
evacuate to in case of emergency. OH SHIT.
my building is literally collapsing. you know
where I'd feel safest? The bathroom. Now
you're a floor-to-floor sandwich. Want to
escape the bathroom? Yeah. Go ahead.
Now your hand is covered in filth from the
doorhandle because some geniuses think
they're too good to wash their hands after
releasing a boat horn into the toilet. so I ask
WHY THE FUCK IS EVERY BATHROOM
DOOR A PULL DOOR?!?
